```{r setup}
}

library(rvg)

source(knitr::purl(
  "/Users/to909/Desktop/Terlipressin projects/Terlipressin/code/shared_pipeline.qmd",
  quiet = TRUE
))

# Reporting precision: OR/HR and 95% CI to 2 decimals, p-values to 3 decimals.
fmt_estimate <- function(x) gtsummary::style_number(x, digits = 2)
fmt_pvalue   <- function(x) gtsummary::style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)

# Table 1 via tableone with every value at 3 decimals; writes the CSV and returns the same matrix.
tableone_3dp <- function(vars, cat_vars, data, strata, output) {
  t1 <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
    vars = vars, strata = strata, data = data,
    factorVars = cat_vars, addOverall = TRUE, includeNA = FALSE
  )
  out <- print(
    t1, showAllLevels = TRUE, nonnormal = setdiff(vars, cat_vars),
    missing = TRUE, quote = FALSE, noSpaces = TRUE, printToggle = FALSE,
    catDigits = 3, contDigits = 3, pDigits = 3
  )
  # print() always formats Missing at 1 decimal, so recompute it from the data
  miss_rows <- which(out[, "Missing"] != "")
  stopifnot(length(miss_rows) == length(vars))
  out[miss_rows, "Missing"] <- sprintf("%.3f", 100 * colMeans(is.na(data[vars])))
  write.csv(out, file = output, row.names = TRUE)
  knitr::kable(out)
}

# Save a single ggplot to docs/plots/<slug>.pptx (one slide).
# Tries editable vector graphics via rvg::dml() first, falls back to a PNG
# snapshot for compound plots (e.g. ggsurvfit + risktable patchwork) that
# the rvg pptx device can't paginate. Returns the plot so the caller can
# print it inline.
save_plot_pptx <- function(slug, plot, title = slug) {
  dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  loc <- ph_location(left = 0.5, top = 1.3, width = 9.0, height = 5.5)

  ppt <- read_pptx() %>%
    add_slide(layout = "Title and Content", master = "Office Theme") %>%
    ph_with(value = title, location = ph_location_type("title"))

  ppt <- tryCatch(
    ph_with(ppt, value = dml(ggobj = plot, bg = "transparent"), location = loc),
    error = function(e) {
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
      ggsave(tmp, plot = plot, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
      ph_with(ppt, value = external_img(tmp, width = 9.0, height = 5.5), location = loc)
    }
  )

  print(ppt, target = file.path("plots", paste0(slug, ".pptx")))
  plot
}
```

```{r helpers}
#| include: false
# Predict adjusted CIF curves for AH vs non-AH from a riskRegression::FGR fit.
# Continuous covariates are held at their median; factor covariates at their
# modal level. The exposure variable is varied across its levels.
adjusted_cif <- function(formula, data, exposure = "etoh_hepatitis",
                         times = 0:90,
                         cause = 1) {           # cause = 1 -> Death (outcome of interest)
                                                # cause = 2 -> Transplant (competing risk)
  fg <- riskRegression::FGR(formula, data = data, cause = cause)

  covars <- setdiff(all.vars(formula)[-c(1, 2)], exposure)
  profile <- lapply(covars, function(v) {
    x <- data[[v]]
    if (is.numeric(x)) {
      median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      lvls <- levels(factor(x))
      modal <- names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
      factor(modal, levels = lvls)
    }
  })
  names(profile) <- covars
  # Keep the fitted factor levels; a character column is re-levelled alphabetically and swaps the groups.
  profile[[exposure]] <- factor(levels(data[[exposure]]), levels = levels(data[[exposure]]))
  newdata <- do.call(expand.grid, c(profile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

  risk <- riskRegression::predictRisk(fg, newdata = newdata, times = times)
  colnames(risk) <- times

  as.data.frame(risk) |>
    dplyr::mutate(!!exposure := as.character(newdata[[exposure]])) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-dplyr::all_of(exposure),
                        names_to = "time", values_to = "cif") |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = as.numeric(time))
}

plot_adjusted_cif <- function(df, exposure = "etoh_hepatitis",
                              title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = cif,
                 color = .data[[exposure]], linetype = .data[[exposure]])) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 90, by = 30),
                       limits = c(0, 90),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = "Days from terlipressin initiation",
         y = "Adjusted CIF  -  Death",
         color = "Alcoholic hepatitis",
         linetype = "Alcoholic hepatitis",
         title = title,
         subtitle = subtitle,
         caption = "Outcome: death (cause 1)  |  Competing risk: liver transplant (cause 2)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.caption = element_text(face = "italic"))
}
```

## Analysis Cohort

`master` comes from the shared pipeline. Throughout this analysis:

- **Exposure:** `etoh_hepatitis`  -  alcoholic hepatitis (AH) vs. non-AH
- **Primary outcome (event of interest, cause = 1):** death within 90 days
- **Competing risk (cause = 2):** liver transplant within 90 days
- **Censoring (cause = 0):** alive and not transplanted at 90 days / lost to follow-up

Time and status come from the shared pipeline variables `time_to_death_90days_cmp` / `time_to_death_status_90days_cmp` (0 = censored, 1 = death, 2 = transplant).

```{r cohort}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show cohort filter"
# Cause coding for the competing-risk event factor `event_cmp`:
#   level 1 "Censored"   -> censoring        (numeric code 0)
#   level 2 "Death"      -> OUTCOME OF INTEREST (numeric code 1)
#   level 3 "Transplant" -> COMPETING RISK   (numeric code 2)
# This ordering matters: tidycmprsk::crr() treats the first level as the
# censoring code, and `failcode` selects which remaining level is the cause
# of interest (all other non-censoring levels become competing risks).
analysis <- master %>%
  filter(!is.na(etoh_hepatitis)) %>%
  mutate(
    etoh_hepatitis = factor(etoh_hepatitis, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Non-AH", "AH")),
    event_cmp      = factor(time_to_death_status_90days_cmp,
                            levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                            labels = c("Censored", "Death", "Transplant"))
  )
```

## Unadjusted Fine-Gray  -  90-day mortality (AH vs. non-AH)

**Outcome:** death within 90 days (cause 1) &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Competing risk:** liver transplant (cause 2)

```{r fg-unadj}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show unadjusted Fine-Gray"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
# Outcome of interest = "Death"; competing risk = "Transplant"
# (`failcode` is matched against the levels of `event_cmp`).
fg_unadj <- tidycmprsk::crr(
  Surv(time_to_death_90days_cmp, event_cmp) ~ etoh_hepatitis,
  data     = analysis,
  failcode = "Death"   # cause of interest -> all other non-censoring levels are competing risks
)

fg_unadj %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE,
                 estimate_fun = fmt_estimate,
                 pvalue_fun   = fmt_pvalue) %>%
  modify_caption(
    "Unadjusted subdistribution hazard ratio  -  Outcome: death (cause 1); Competing risk: liver transplant (cause 2)"
  )

# Aalen-Johansen non-parametric CIF (used for both the plot and the day-90 estimates below)
ci_unadj <- cuminc(
  Surv(time_to_death_90days_cmp, event_cmp) ~ etoh_hepatitis,
  data = analysis
)

p_unadj <- ci_unadj %>%
  ggcuminc(outcome = "Death") +
  labs(
    title    = "Unadjusted 90-day cumulative incidence of death",
    subtitle = "AH vs. non-AH",
    x        = "Days from terlipressin initiation",
    y        = "Cumulative incidence  -  Death",
    caption  = "Outcome: death (cause 1)  |  Competing risk: liver transplant (cause 2)"
  ) +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable(
    risktable_stats  = c("n.risk", "cum.event"),
    stats_label      = list(n.risk = "At risk", cum.event = "Events"),
    risktable_height = 0.30,
    size             = 3.2,
    theme = theme_risktable_default(
      axis.text.y.size = 9,
      plot.title.size  = 10
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 90, by = 30),
    limits = c(0, 90),
    # Push the day-0 column ~3 days inside the panel so the leftmost
    # numbers don't overlap the "At risk" / "Events" row labels.
    expand = expansion(add = c(3, 1))
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(face = "italic"),
    plot.margin  = margin(5, 10, 5, 15)   # extra left margin
  )

save_plot_pptx("unadjusted_cif", p_unadj,
               "Unadjusted 90-day cumulative incidence of death (AH vs. non-AH)")
```

### 90-day cumulative incidence of death (AH vs. non-AH)

Non-parametric **Aalen-Johansen** estimator at *t* = 90 days, accounting for liver transplant as a competing risk. 95% CIs use the log-log transformation.

```{r ci90-table}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show 90-day CIF table"
ci90_raw <- ci_unadj %>%
  tidy(times = 90) %>%
  filter(outcome == "Death")

ci90_raw %>%
  transmute(
    Group              = strata,
    `CIF at 90d (%)`   = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * estimate),
    `95% CI (%)`       = sprintf("%.1f - %.1f", 100 * conf.low, 100 * conf.high)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    align   = "lrr",
    caption = "Aalen-Johansen 90-day cumulative incidence of death (competing risk: liver transplant)."
  )
```

```{r ci90-sentence}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show inline sentence"
#| results: asis
ah  <- ci90_raw %>% filter(strata == "AH")
nah <- ci90_raw %>% filter(strata == "Non-AH")

cat(glue::glue(
  "At 90 days the cumulative incidence of death accounting for liver transplant ",
  "as a competing risk was **{sprintf('%.1f', 100*ah$estimate)}%** in the AH group ",
  "(95% CI {sprintf('%.1f', 100*ah$conf.low)}-{sprintf('%.1f', 100*ah$conf.high)}) ",
  "and **{sprintf('%.1f', 100*nah$estimate)}%** in the non-AH group ",
  "(95% CI {sprintf('%.1f', 100*nah$conf.low)}-{sprintf('%.1f', 100*nah$conf.high)})."
))
```

## Adjusted Fine-Gray  -  MELD 3.0 model

**Outcome:** death within 90 days (cause 1) &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Competing risk:** liver transplant (cause 2)
&nbsp;|&nbsp; **Covariates:** `age`, `sex_male`, `hispanic`, `admit_meld_3`, `etoh_hepatitis`.

```{r fg-meld3}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show MELD 3.0 adjusted Fine-Gray"
# Outcome of interest = "Death"; competing risk = "Transplant"
tidycmprsk::crr(
  Surv(time_to_death_90days_cmp, event_cmp) ~
    age + sex_male + hispanic + admit_meld_3 + etoh_hepatitis,
  data     = analysis,
  failcode = "Death"   # competing risk: "Transplant"
) %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE,
                 estimate_fun = fmt_estimate,
                 pvalue_fun   = fmt_pvalue) %>%
  modify_caption(
    "Adjusted (MELD 3.0) subdistribution hazard ratio  -  Outcome: death (cause 1); Competing risk: liver transplant (cause 2)"
  )
```

```{r fg-meld3-cif}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show adjusted CIF (MELD 3.0 model)"
cif_meld3 <- adjusted_cif(
  prodlim::Hist(time_to_death_90days_cmp, time_to_death_status_90days_cmp) ~
    age + sex_male + hispanic + admit_meld_3 + etoh_hepatitis,
  data = analysis
)

save_plot_pptx(
  "adjusted_meld3",
  plot_adjusted_cif(
    cif_meld3,
    title    = "Adjusted 90-day CIF of death  -  MELD 3.0 model",
    subtitle = "Continuous covariates at median, categoricals at modal level"
  ),
  "Adjusted CIF (MELD 3.0 model)"
)
```

# Reference model (no exposure): `age` + `admit_meld_3`

Same Fine-Gray specification with `etoh_hepatitis` removed entirely. This is a population-level reference: the AH vs non-AH comparison is gone, and the CIF plot shows a single curve for a typical patient (median age, median admit MELD 3.0).

## Adjusted Fine-Gray  -  age + admit_meld_3 (no exposure)

**Outcome:** death within 90 days (cause 1) &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Competing risk:** liver transplant (cause 2)
&nbsp;|&nbsp; **Covariates:** `age`, `admit_meld_3`. **Exposure:** *none.*

```{r fg-noexp}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show no-exposure Fine-Gray"
# No exposure variable - this is a population reference model.
tidycmprsk::crr(
  Surv(time_to_death_90days_cmp, event_cmp) ~ age + admit_meld_3,
  data     = analysis,
  failcode = "Death"
) %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE,
                 estimate_fun = fmt_estimate,
                 pvalue_fun   = fmt_pvalue) %>%
  modify_caption(
    "No-exposure subdistribution hazard ratio (age + admit_meld_3)  -  Outcome: death (cause 1); Competing risk: liver transplant (cause 2)"
  )
```

# Binary logistic regression - HRS overall response

Two multivariable binary logistic regression models for overall HRS response (`hrs_responders_cat_2`, 1 = responder / 0 = non-responder). Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

```{r lr-setup}
#| include: false
# Re-cast the outcome and any factor covariates to the forms glm() expects.
# `hrs_responders_cat_2` is set as a factor in the Table 1 chunk; glm with
# family = binomial() accepts a 0/1 numeric or a 2-level factor, but cast to
# numeric here so the reference level is explicitly 0.
analysis_lr <- analysis %>%
  mutate(
    hrs_responders_cat_2 = as.numeric(as.character(hrs_responders_cat_2)),
    # Grade 0 has no non-responders (complete separation), so it is merged into grade 1 as the reference.
    aclf_grade           = factor(if_else(aclf_grade <= 1, "0-1", as.character(aclf_grade)),
                                  levels = c("0-1", "2", "3")),
    sex_male             = factor(sex_male),
    etoh_hepatitis       = factor(etoh_hepatitis, levels = c("Non-AH", "AH"))
  )
```

## Model 1: age + sex_male + etoh_hepatitis + aclf_grade

**Outcome:** `hrs_responders_cat_2` (1 = responder, 0 = non-responder).
**Predictors:** `age`, `sex_male`, `etoh_hepatitis`, `aclf_grade` (0-1, 2, 3; reference = 0-1).

::: {.callout-note}
## ACLF grade 0 merged into grade 1

In this model, ACLF grades 0 and 1 are combined into a single reference category (ACLF 0-1). Every patient with ACLF grade 0 (n < 11) was an HRS responder, so with grade 0 as its own reference level the model could not estimate the grade 1-3 odds ratios (complete separation; they appeared as OR 0.00 with no confidence interval). The Fine-Gray models are unaffected; they use `aclf_grade` as a continuous term.
:::

```{r lr-model1}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show LR Model 1"
glm(
  hrs_responders_cat_2 ~ age + sex_male + etoh_hepatitis + aclf_grade,
  data   = analysis_lr,
  family = binomial()
) %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE,
                 estimate_fun = fmt_estimate,
                 pvalue_fun   = fmt_pvalue) %>%
  modify_caption(
    "Multivariable LR Model 1 (age + sex_male + etoh_hepatitis + aclf_grade)  -  Outcome: hrs_responders_cat_2"
  )
```

## Model 2: age + etoh_hepatitis + day0_meld

**Outcome:** `hrs_responders_cat_2` (1 = responder, 0 = non-responder).
**Predictors:** `age`, `etoh_hepatitis`, `day0_meld`.

```{r lr-model2}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show LR Model 2"
glm(
  hrs_responders_cat_2 ~ age + etoh_hepatitis + day0_meld,
  data   = analysis_lr,
  family = binomial()
) %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE,
                 estimate_fun = fmt_estimate,
                 pvalue_fun   = fmt_pvalue) %>%
  modify_caption(
    "Multivariable LR Model 2 (age + etoh_hepatitis + day0_meld)  -  Outcome: hrs_responders_cat_2"
  )
```

# Flow diagram - HRS response in AH vs non-AH

**Cohort:** all patients with known `etoh_hepatitis` (n = 242), drawn as two left-to-right diagrams: non-AH (`etoh_hepatitis = 0`) and AH (`etoh_hepatitis = 1`).

- **Column 1:** the `etoh_hepatitis` group.
- **Column 2:** HRS response, `hrs_responders_cat_2` = 0 (non-responders) or 1 (responders).
- **Column 3:** RRT during the index hospitalization: `rrt = 1` (RRT) or `rrt = 0 or 2` (no RRT; 2 = needed RRT but not a candidate).
- **Column 4 (90-day outcomes):** within each RRT group, patients who died (`time_to_death_status = 1`), received a liver transplant (`transplant_lt_status = 1 or 2`) or were on RRT at 90 days (`efu_90_rrt = 1`). A patient can have more than one outcome.

`efu_90_rrt` is not in the master dataset. It comes from the extended follow-up (EFU) site files (09SEP2026 export), joined on a normalized study ID as in the Liver transplant sub-project. It is missing for the 21 CSF patients (CSF has no EFU file) and for patients whose 90-day RRT field was left blank, mostly those who died before day 90. `transplant_lt_status` is coded 0/2, so `= 1 or 2` counts every liver transplant recorded through 1-year follow-up.

```{r flow-efu}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show extended follow-up join"
# EFU writes Yale IDs as YAL-00N while the master uses Yale-N, so join on a normalized ID.
norm_id <- function(x) {
  x      <- str_trim(x)
  prefix <- toupper(str_extract(x, "^[A-Za-z]+"))
  prefix <- if_else(prefix == "YAL", "YALE", prefix)
  paste0(prefix, "-", as.integer(str_extract(x, "[0-9]+$")))
}

efu <- list.files(
  "/Users/to909/Partners HealthCare Dropbox/Tianqi Ouyang/Extended Data Collection/Finalized Files/09SEP2026",
  pattern = "_09092026\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE
) %>%
  map_dfr(~ read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE)) %>%
  transmute(id_key = norm_id(subjectid), efu_90_rrt = as.integer(efu_90_rrt))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(efu$id_key))

analysis_flow <- analysis %>%
  mutate(id_key = norm_id(subjectid)) %>%
  left_join(efu, by = "id_key")

tibble(
  `Cohort patients`     = nrow(analysis_flow),
  `With an EFU record`  = sum(analysis_flow$id_key %in% efu$id_key),
  `efu_90_rrt recorded` = sum(!is.na(analysis_flow$efu_90_rrt))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Extended follow-up (EFU) join")
```

```{r flow-helpers}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show flow-diagram code"
flow_counts <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      resp    = as.character(hrs_responders_cat_2),
      rrt_grp = case_when(as.numeric(rrt) == 1 ~ "RRT", as.numeric(rrt) %in% c(0, 2) ~ "No RRT")
    )
  stopifnot(!anyNA(df$rrt_grp))
  df %>%
    group_by(resp, rrt_grp) %>%
    summarise(
      n          = n(),
      death      = sum(time_to_death_status == 1),
      lt         = sum(transplant_lt_status %in% c(1, 2)),
      rrt90      = sum(efu_90_rrt == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      rrt90_miss = sum(is.na(efu_90_rrt)),
      .groups    = "drop"
    )
}

mix_white <- function(col, p) {
  m <- grDevices::col2rgb(col) * (1 - p) + 255 * p
  grDevices::rgb(m[1, ], m[2, ], m[3, ], maxColorValue = 255)
}

rounded_box <- function(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, r = 1.2, n = 8) {
  a <- seq(0, pi / 2, length.out = n)
  tibble(x = c(xmax - r + r * cos(a), xmin + r - r * sin(a), xmin + r - r * cos(a), xmax - r + r * sin(a)),
         y = c(ymax - r + r * sin(a), ymax - r + r * cos(a), ymin + r - r * sin(a), ymin + r - r * cos(a)))
}

# Constant-width band whose centre line follows a smoothstep curve from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1).
ribbon <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1, hw = 2.2, n = 60) {
  t  <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  x  <- x0 + (x1 - x0) * t
  yc <- y0 + (y1 - y0) * (3 * t^2 - 2 * t^3)
  tibble(x = c(x, rev(x)), y = c(yc + hw, rev(yc - hw)))
}

# Sized for the 9 x 5.5 in figure, which is also the .pptx placement, so text fits in both.
plot_flow <- function(counts, root_label) {
  counts <- counts %>%
    complete(resp = c("0", "1"), rrt_grp = c("RRT", "No RRT"),
             fill = list(n = 0L, death = 0L, lt = 0L, rrt90 = 0L, rrt90_miss = 0L))
  y_leaf <- c(52, 37, 22, 7)
  y_resp <- c(mean(y_leaf[1:2]), mean(y_leaf[3:4]))
  y_root <- mean(y_resp)

  leaf <- tibble(resp = c("0", "0", "1", "1"), rrt_grp = c("RRT", "No RRT", "RRT", "No RRT"), y = y_leaf,
                 fill = c("#f9cfca", "#dbe8f9", "#fcdcc9", "#e0f2db"),
                 line = c("#d9534a", "#4a83d6", "#e8773a", "#5aa64f")) %>%
    left_join(counts, by = c("resp", "rrt_grp"))
  resp_n <- c(sum(counts$n[counts$resp == "0"]), sum(counts$n[counts$resp == "1"]))

  nodes <- bind_rows(
    tibble(xmin = 1, xmax = 16, y = y_root, h = 13, fill = "#e3e3e3", line = "#666666",
           title = root_label, count = paste0("(n = ", sum(counts$n), ")"),
           tsize = 4.3, csize = 4.0, tdy = 2.0, cdy = -2.2),
    tibble(xmin = 24, xmax = 43, y = y_resp, h = 10, fill = c("#d6e4f7", "#d8eed2"), line = c("#2f5fa8", "#2e7d32"),
           title = c("Non-responders", "Responders"), count = paste0("(n = ", resp_n, ")"),
           tsize = 3.9, csize = 3.7, tdy = 1.8, cdy = -2.0),
    leaf %>% transmute(xmin = 50, xmax = 70, y, h = 10, fill, line,
                       title = if_else(rrt_grp == "RRT", "RRT during\nhospitalization", "No RRT during\nhospitalization"),
                       count = paste0("(n = ", n, ")"), tsize = 3.3, csize = 3.3, tdy = 1.4, cdy = -3.0)
  )
  outs <- leaf %>% transmute(xmin = 76, xmax = 110, y, h = 12.5,
                             fill = mix_white(fill, 0.55), line = mix_white(line, 0.35),
                             death, lt, rrt90, rrt90_miss)

  boxes <- bind_rows(nodes, outs) %>%
    mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
    pmap_dfr(function(id, xmin, xmax, y, h, fill, line, ...) {
      rounded_box(xmin, xmax, y - h / 2, y + h / 2) %>% mutate(id = id, fill = fill, line = line)
    })

  edges <- bind_rows(
    tibble(x0 = 15, y0 = y_root + c(3, -3), x1 = 25, y1 = y_resp, col = c("#2f5fa8", "#2e7d32")),
    tibble(x0 = 42, y0 = rep(y_resp, each = 2) + c(2.7, -2.7, 2.7, -2.7), x1 = 51, y1 = y_leaf, col = leaf$line),
    tibble(x0 = 69, y0 = y_leaf, x1 = 77, y1 = y_leaf, col = leaf$line)
  )
  ribbons <- edges %>%
    mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
    pmap_dfr(function(x0, y0, x1, y1, col, id) {
      ribbon(x0, y0, x1, y1) %>% mutate(id = id, fill = mix_white(col, 0.55))
    })

  # Blue darkened and purple lightened vs the mock-up so they stay distinct with colour-vision deficiency.
  out_colours <- c("#e5534b", "#1f5fbf", "#c084d8")
  out_rows <- outs %>%
    mutate(box = row_number()) %>%
    reframe(
      x = xmin, y = y + c(3.4, 0, -3.4), colour = out_colours,
      label = c(paste0("Death: n = ", death), paste0("Liver transplant: n = ", lt),
                paste0("RRT at 90 days: n = ", rrt90, " (missing: ", rrt90_miss, ")")),
      .by = box
    )

  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = ribbons, aes(x, y, group = id, fill = fill), colour = NA) +
    geom_polygon(data = boxes, aes(x, y, group = id, fill = fill, colour = line), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = nodes, aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y + tdy, label = title, size = tsize),
              fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9, colour = "#1f1f1f") +
    geom_text(data = nodes, aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y + cdy, label = count, size = csize),
              colour = "#1f1f1f") +
    geom_rect(data = out_rows, aes(xmin = x + 1.6, xmax = x + 3.1, ymin = y - 0.75, ymax = y + 0.75, fill = colour)) +
    geom_text(data = out_rows, aes(x = x + 4.1, y = y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 3.1, colour = "#262626") +
    annotate("text", x = 93, y = 61.3, label = "90-day outcomes", fontface = "bold", size = 4.3, colour = "#1f1f1f") +
    scale_fill_identity() + scale_colour_identity() + scale_size_identity() +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 111), ylim = c(0, 64), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(caption = paste0(
      "RRT during hospitalization: rrt = 1 (no RRT: rrt = 0 or 2). Death: time_to_death_status = 1. ",
      "Liver transplant: transplant_lt_status = 1 or 2 (through 1-year follow-up).\n",
      "RRT at 90 days: efu_90_rrt = 1 from the extended follow-up (missing = no EFU record or field left blank). ",
      "A patient can have more than one outcome.")) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey30", hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.1),
          plot.margin  = margin(6, 6, 6, 6))
}
```
